quotes.text: Treating OE as a root cause answer is like treating a warning light as a repair manual. It tells you where to look. It doesn't tell you what to change.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable analogy for why headline metrics like OEE do not diagnose causes.

quotes.text: If not, they adapt or stop it. Stopping a weak countermeasure isn't failure. It's preventing a weak habit from becoming standard.

quotes.text: Real-time data can help, but it isn't a badge of seriousness. A late but trusted record can beat a live number with no production context.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Challenges the reflex to demand real-time data for every improvement question.

quotes.text: That consistency matters more than visual polish. A clean report with unclear logic just speeds up disagreement.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: A data defect is a process defect. Something in the method, system, interface, or definition let the record drift away from the work.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Treats data quality as part of standard work rather than an IT cleanup task.

chapters.title: PDCA needs a reliable check step
ERP, MES, machine data and the shop floor
The data model behind continuous improvement

takeaways: Continuous improvement stalls when the PDCA check step lacks connected evidence, because completed actions are not the same as learning.
ERP shows intent, MES shows execution, machine data shows physical behavior and operators add meaning, so improvement needs all four linked through a shared data model.
Microsoft Azure, Fabric and Power BI can carry that evidence chain, but the factory itself must define what a stop, a changeover or good output means.
hook: Kaizen workshops often feel like progress, yet the same losses return a few weeks later. This episode is for lean leaders, plant engineers and manufacturing IT teams who want continuous improvement that lasts. Learn how to connect ERP, MES, machine data and shop-floor knowledge into a reliable PDCA check step that shows which countermeasures actually hold.
